principle.name: Zero Tolerance for Security Vulnerabilities
principle.description: Any security vulnerability, regardless of severity, must halt the review process immediately. No code with security issues should ever be committed or pushed.
principle.rationale: Security vulnerabilities can lead to data breaches, unauthorized access, and catastrophic system failures. They must be identified and fixed before deployment.

principle.name: All Tests Must Pass
principle.description: Every test in the suite must pass successfully before any code can be committed. A single failing test is a blocker for the entire review.
principle.rationale: Failing tests indicate broken functionality or regressions. Committing code with failing tests undermines confidence in the codebase and can introduce bugs to production.
principle.exceptions: Only if the test itself is identified as the issue (not the code), and even then, the test must be fixed before proceeding.

principle.name: Comprehensive Test Coverage
principle.description: New code must have corresponding tests that cover all significant paths, edge cases, and error conditions.
principle.rationale: Without adequate test coverage, code behavior is unverified and prone to unexpected failures in production. Tests serve as living documentation.
principle.exceptions: Trivial changes like comments, whitespace, or documentation-only updates may not require new tests.

principle.name: Consistency with Project Standards
principle.description: Code must follow established project conventions for naming, structure, formatting, and architectural patterns.
principle.rationale: Consistency improves maintainability, reduces cognitive load for developers, and prevents subtle bugs from inconsistent patterns.
principle.exceptions: Only if the existing standard is being intentionally refactored as part of the changes being reviewed.

principle.name: Performance Awareness
principle.description: Code should be reviewed for potential performance bottlenecks, inefficient algorithms, or resource management issues.
principle.rationale: Performance issues compound over time and can lead to poor user experience, increased infrastructure costs, and system instability.
principle.exceptions: When performance optimizations would significantly increase complexity or reduce readability, a trade-off discussion may be warranted.

principle.name: Clear and Constructive Feedback
principle.description: All critique must be specific, actionable, and focused on the code, not the person who wrote it.
principle.rationale: Constructive feedback helps developers improve and fosters a positive development culture. Personal criticism creates defensiveness and hinders collaboration.

convention.rule: Follow language and framework naming conventions

good.example: camelCase for variables and functions, PascalCase for classes
snake_case for variables and functions, PascalCase for classes
camelCase for exported, PascalCase for types

convention.rule: Organize code logically and follow separation of concerns

guidelines.guideline: Keep functions focused and small (single responsibility)
Use clear file and directory organization

convention.rule: Document non-obvious code and public APIs

guidelines.guideline: Keep comments up-to-date with code changes
Avoid commenting obvious code (self-documenting code is better)
Use appropriate error types and messages

category.name: input_validation

Type checking is performed on all inputs

category.item: Passwords are never stored in plain text
API keys and secrets use environment variables
PII (Personally Identifiable Information) is handled appropriately

Token handling follows security best practices
Rate limiting is implemented where appropriate

category.name: database_operations
category.item: Pagination is implemented for large result sets
Connection pooling is used where appropriate

category.name: algorithm_efficiency
category.item: Time complexity is appropriate for the problem
Caching is used for expensive operations

category.item: File handles and connections are properly closed

pitfall.why_problematic: Code that mostly works often has edge cases that will fail in production. These failures are harder to debug and more costly to fix later.
pitfall.correct_approach: Require comprehensive testing and thorough review before accepting any code. If edge cases are identified, they must be tested and handled.

pitfall.why_problematic: Quick reviews miss subtle bugs, security issues, and design problems. The cost of fixing issues in production far exceeds the cost of thorough review.
pitfall.correct_approach: Take the time to understand the full context of changes. Review related files and consider the impact on the entire system.

pitfall.description: Being too lenient on coding standards
pitfall.why_problematic: Inconsistent code becomes harder to maintain over time. Technical debt accumulates and slows down future development.
pitfall.correct_approach: Enforce project coding standards consistently. If standards need improvement, address that separately from code reviews.

pitfall.why_problematic: Vague feedback like "this looks wrong" or "refactor this" doesn't help developers understand what needs to change or why.
pitfall.correct_approach: Be specific: "This function has a potential null reference on line 42. Consider adding a null check or using optional chaining."
